question: Is fully explicit main/q execution approximately equal or materially better/worse in complete Policy 4 requests on this host?
baseline: mode 0: ProductionSearch.create Policy 4, recursive main and qsearch
candidate: mode 2: same factory then withFlatSearchResearch(true); primitive explicit main/q continuations, existing TT/helpers/evaluator/ROOT_REUSE. Inactive research branches are excluded by validated construction guards; effect is candidate architecture plus specialization, not isolated call overhead.
artifactBinding: confirmation-v1-binding.json must freeze source and runtime hashes after integrity gates and before execution; no source refinement during this protocol
sampling: First 20 game groups from existing sr021 fresh-diagnostic-corpus.tsv, one root per group at offset gameIndex modulo 3 (8/16/24 played plies). Preserve real history; frozen confirmation-corpus.tsv and source hash in binding. These are fresh to this candidate comparison, not novel positions to the repository.
perDomain: Two sequential independent JVM forks, each two full warmup passes and four measured rounds over all 20 roots. Both modes in each pair, order alternates by round+root index. Depth ceiling 20, exactly at most 1000000 admitted nodes per request. Global 60-second/request safety deadline and 30-minute/process timeout; any time-censored observation invalidates the affected cost comparison, preserved without favorable replacement.
resources: One BelowNormal JVM, OpenJDK 21+35-2513, ActiveProcessorCount=2, Xms256m Xmx768m, 64 MiB requested TT per owner, fresh newGame before each request. No profiling or simultaneous Gradle/tests/benchmarks. Desktop activity is uncontrolled and remains a limitation; process CPU and alternate order reduce but do not eliminate sensitivity.
metrics: Primary paired whole-request elapsed ratio; all-worker process CPU, total nodes/qnodes, completed work, allocation, GC and compilation are co-metrics. New-game clearing is separately recorded; construction excluded. One-worker complete outcomes must match exactly. Multiworker legal publication, total budgets, complete accounting and draining are required; parallel schedule-dependent outcomes are not required to match.
analysis: Equal-weight mean log flat/recursive ratios by game-root, averaging all rounds and forks within each root. 10000 deterministic seed-200219 percentile bootstrap resamples root clusters, preserving within-root observations. Report approximate 95% intervals, per-fork estimates and aggregate cost sensitivity. Never pool worker domains. Fixed corpus, desktop contention and two forks limit generalization.
decision: An interval wholly within [0.95,1.05] supports approximate practical equality, favoring flattened architecture if correctness, memory and engineering costs are acceptable. An interval wholly below 0.95 or above 1.05 supports a meaningful gain or loss in that metric/domain. Disagreement across domains/metrics or boundary-crossing intervals requires an explicit qualified or inconclusive conclusion; 5% is indicative, not an automatic adoption rule. No Elo claim or automatic promotion.
stop: Fixed sample; no interim selection and no result-conditioned extension. Correctness failure stops interpretation and requires remediation/new protocol; external interruption retains partial evidence, not futility. After this protocol, profiling and predetermined fixed-depth/lifecycle checks may diagnose limitations, but cannot be pooled into confirmation. Further architectural refinement only if expected decision value justifies a new separately identified development unit. Otherwise reach the Contract's bounded recommendation/fallback.
additionalChecks: Separate profiled one- and four-worker runs; fixed-depth 6 complete requests capped at 2000000 nodes across the frozen roots (report incomplete cases); core TT/rules and independent Search regression suites. No games are required for a semantics-preserving mechanical comparison.
